label: I q.19 a.1 co. and ad 2 — Seeking or resting in the intellectually apprehended good belongs to will
locator: I q.19 a.1 co. and ad 2
interpretation: The analogy with a thing’s orientation to its natural perfection supports will in an intellectual nature and its application to God. In God the text ascribes love and delight in the possessed good, with no deficiency implied. I q.80 a.2 describes passive appetite in the soul. I q.82 a.1 ad 2 calls will intellectual insofar as it wills something naturally. That reply starts with will already in view.
attribution: The passage states that an intellectual nature stands to its apprehended good so as to seek it when absent and rest in it when possessed and that both belong to will, which is the premise.
